actions.q: Can I use UTMA funds to pay for college?

fact_basis.fact: UTMA: any purpose the custodian (then child) chooses; custodian controls until majority, then child owns it fully (18 to 21, up to 25 in some states)
UTMA counts as the student's asset, assessed at 20% on FAFSA; parent-owned 529 assessed up to 5.64%; $50,000 saved adds about $10,000 vs $2,820
Kiddie tax: unearned income above $2,700 taxed at parents' rate (2025); selling holdings can trigger capital gains
fact_basis.source: page: tax section + 'Can I convert a UTMA to a 529' FAQ

actions.task: Append FAQ 'Can I use UTMA funds to pay for college?' (80-110 words): yes, nothing restricts the money to education (it belongs to the child; spending must be for their benefit); but there is no tax shelter (selling holdings can create taxable gains under the kiddie tax), it counts as a student asset at 20% on the FAFSA vs up to 5.64% for a parent-owned 529, and at majority the child, not the parent, decides how it is spent. End with a link to [UTMA custodial account explained](/guides/utma-custodial-account-explained/). No new figures beyond those listed.
